rules.title: Texas Voting Leave

result.summary: Paid time off to vote unless the employee has 2 consecutive non-working hours while polls are open

citations.source: Tex. Elec. Code §276.004 (50-state survey used for encoding)

rules.title: USERRA — Uniformed Services Leave and Reemployment

params.service_type: uniformed services (active duty, reserve and National Guard federal duty, training)

result.summary: All employers must grant unpaid leave for service in the uniformed services and reemploy the employee in the escalator position after up to 5 cumulative years of service, with no discrimination or retaliation; health coverage continues up to 24 months at the employee's expense. State-ordered National Guard duty is covered only by state law.

rules.title: Texas — State Military Leave and Reemployment

params.service_type: state active duty and National Guard or state militia service

result.summary: Unpaid leave for state military forces training or duty with reinstatement and no loss of time, efficiency rating, vacation or benefits; USERRA-equivalent for state active duty. (Survey-based encoding; dates not researched.)

citations.source: Workplace Fairness, State Laws on Military Leave (50-state survey, used for encoding)
Paycor, Military Leave Laws by State (survey used for encoding)

rules.title: Federal Minimum Wage (FLSA)

result.summary: $7.25 per hour minimum wage

rules.title: Texas Minimum Wage ($7.25/hr)

result.summary: $7.25 per hour minimum wage

rules.title: Federal Weekly Overtime (FLSA)

result.summary: 1.5x regular rate for hours over 40 in a week

rules.title: Federal Workweek Definition (FLSA)

result.summary: Overtime is computed over a fixed and regularly recurring period of 168 hours (seven consecutive 24-hour periods) that may begin on any day and hour; it may be changed only permanently and not to evade overtime, and hours may not be averaged across weeks

rules.title: Federal — EAP Exemption Salary Level $684/week (29 CFR 541.600)

result.summary: An executive, administrative or professional employee is exempt from FLSA overtime only if paid on a salary basis at least $684 a week ($35,568 a year), plus $107,432 total annual compensation for the highly compensated employee test. The 2024 rule raising these levels was vacated (E.D. Tex. 2024-11-15) and formally rescinded by DOL on 2026-05-15, so the 2019 levels remain in force. States may set higher thresholds.

rules.title: Texas — Pay Frequency

result.summary: Non-exempt employees must be paid at least twice a month on paydays with roughly equal periods; FLSA-exempt employees at least monthly.

rules.title: FLSA — Wage Deductions

result.summary: Under the FLSA, deductions for items that primarily benefit the employer (uniforms, tools, cash shortages, damage) may not reduce pay below the minimum wage or cut into overtime.

citations.source: 29 CFR §531.35 (wages must be paid free and clear)
US DOL Fact Sheet #16: Deductions from Wages for Uniforms and Other Facilities

rules.title: Texas — Wage Deductions

params.notes: Wage claims to the Texas Workforce Commission within 180 days; bad-faith penalty up to $1,000

result.summary: Deductions not ordered by a court or authorized by law need the employee's written authorization for a lawful purpose that names the purpose and gives a reasonable expectation of the amount; shortages and damage need the same specific authorization.

citations.source: Ezel, Employee Wage Deduction Requirements by State (survey)

rules.title: Equal Pay Act of 1963 — Equal Pay

params.notes: Covers all FLSA-covered employers; NLRA §7 separately protects most non-supervisory employees who discuss wages

result.summary: Employees of the opposite sex doing equal work (equal skill, effort and responsibility under similar conditions) in the same establishment must be paid equally unless a seniority, merit, production or other factor-other-than-sex system explains the gap.

rules.title: Texas — Equal Pay

params.protected_classes: race, color, disability, religion, sex, national origin, age

result.summary: The Texas Equal Pay Act covers only public employees; private-sector pay discrimination is reached through the Texas Commission on Human Rights Act for employers of 15 or more.

citations.source: Paycor, Pay Equity and State-by-State Laws (survey)

rules.title: Federal Lactation Break Time (PUMP Act)

result.summary: Reasonable break time each time the employee needs to express milk for one year after the child's birth, in a private non-bathroom space; unpaid unless the employee is not fully relieved or uses a paid break (employers under 50 may claim undue hardship)

citations.source: Fair Labor Standards Act §18d (PUMP for Nursing Mothers Act)

rules.title: Texas Retail Employees: One 24-Hour Rest Period in Seven (Labor Code §52.001)

result.summary: An employer whose business is selling merchandise at retail may not require an employee to work seven consecutive days, and may not deny at least one 24-hour period off for rest or worship in each seven-day period; it must also accommodate the employee's weekly worship service absent undue hardship. Part-time employees working 30 or fewer hours a week are excluded. Acts 1993, 73rd Leg., ch. 269.

citations.source: Tex. Labor Code §52.001 (Retail employers — one day of rest in seven)

rules.title: Texas — Final Wages on Discharge

result.summary: Discharged employees are paid in full within 6 calendar days.

rules.title: Texas — Final Wages on Resignation

result.summary: Employees who quit are paid by the next regularly scheduled payday.

params.description: Employers below this size may claim undue hardship (federal: 50)

params.name: minimum_minutes
